clue.text: Supporting what's proposed in meeting for sales campaign

parts.note: to be pro something is to support it
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting for debate and vote

explanation.surface: Backing a proposal at a business meeting about a marketing drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotion is a publicity push designed to boost the sales of a product.

clue.text: The girl's climbing tree? That's nothing really new

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: the girl's means belonging to her, so 'her'
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a girl up a tree is old news.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehash is old material reworked and served up again, offering nothing genuinely fresh.

clue.text: Doctored drink for mouse

definitions.meaning: a ... Finn, often just a ..., is a drink secretly laced with a drug
... Mouse is Disney's famous cartoon mouse

explanation.surface: Spiking a drink to knock out a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipping someone a mickey means drugging their drink; Disney's best-known cartoon rodent bears the same name.

clue.text: Little kid grabs mum having nothing that's suitable to eat

definitions.note: a noun phrase: something that is fit to be eaten

indicators.note: having means the next piece is added on after what comes before
the little kid holds the next piece within its grasp, so it goes inside

parts.note: a tot is a small child
ma is an informal word for mum
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A toddler clutches their mother, with nothing fit to eat in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomato is an edible fruit, one example of food fit for eating.

clue.text: Unfashionable team having emerged from the tunnel?

definitions.note: describes a state: out in the open, no longer in the tunnel

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: An unstylish football team walks out of the players' tunnel onto the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful, hence the question mark: once through the tunnel you are no longer indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming out of a tunnel leaves you in the open air, beyond the enclosed space.

clue.text: Attic poet looking silly in undergarment

indicators.note: looking silly suggests the letters of attic poet are made foolish, jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet in a garret looks ridiculous dressed in underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A petticoat is a slip or underskirt worn beneath a dress.

clue.text: What patient may do before subsequent transplant is despair

definitions.text: What patient may do before subsequent transplant
definitions.meaning: a heart transplant patient first has their own organ removed, so this is a literal reading of the phrase
to give up hope or become discouraged

explanation.surface: A hospital patient gives up hope while waiting for an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part reads the idiom literally: before receiving a new heart, the patient must part with the old one.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is an idiom for becoming discouraged and giving up hope.

clue.text: People primarily wanting freedom? We've heard that before

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of people is used

parts.note: latitude is scope or freedom to act

explanation.surface: Mostly people want liberty, a tired line everyone has heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite remark, said so often it carries no fresh meaning.

clue.text: Draw back from sports ground with slimy liquid

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public playing field in Britain
oil is a greasy, slippery liquid

explanation.surface: Someone shrinks away from a playing field slick with grease.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to flinch or pull away in shock or disgust.

clue.text: Report of European friend in position of defeat

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a Czech mate is a pal from the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: News of a pal from Europe who has been beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the final position in which the king cannot escape capture means the game is lost.

clue.text: Queen beset by an ordeal departed

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the queen is enclosed by the other letters

parts.note: a test is a trying experience, an ordeal
R, for Regina, is the Latin abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A queen suffering through an ordeal has passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At rest' is a euphemism for dead, which 'departed' also is.
explanation.definitionFit: At rest is a gentle euphemism for dead, as is departed when speaking of the deceased.

clue.text: Find out what upsets sectarian

indicators.note: upsets means knocks over, so the letters of sectarian tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks what it is that riles a bigot.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to establish or discover something for certain.

clue.text: Bill with minimal amount of money creates stress

parts.note: AC (or A/C) is short for account, a bill
a cent is the smallest coin in many currencies

explanation.surface: A bill with only pennies to pay it brings on anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' looks like worry, but here it means emphasis on a syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is the emphasis placed on a syllable or word, its stress.

clue.text: Goddess of love could make OAP dither

indicators.note: could make says the letters of OAP dither are re-formed into something new

explanation.surface: The love goddess could fluster a pensioner. OAP means old-age pensioner in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is the deity of love and beauty, counterpart of the Roman Venus.

clue.text: Being awfully mean, one restricts useful services

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so the letters of mean are put in a jumbled order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ties means binds or restricts

explanation.surface: A miser cuts off handy facilities for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' makes AMEN from MEAN. 'Being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are facilities such as shops, parks or libraries that make a place convenient to live in.

clue.text: Soldiers completely capturing small island, as is necessary

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: capturing means taking a prisoner inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: quite can mean entirely, completely
Is. is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Troops seize a tiny isle because it must be done.
explanation.definitionFit: Requisite describes something required or essential for a purpose.

clue.text: Stone Margaret's turned over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Meg is a pet form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: A stone belonging to Margaret has been flipped.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret's is Margaret is: the name is what gets turned.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem is a precious stone, cut and polished for jewellery.

clue.text: Some begging for a drink

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters are found within the word begging

explanation.surface: Someone pleading for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin is a spirit flavoured with juniper berries.

clue.text: Female invited into garden not wanting a soft soil

indicators.note: not wanting means doing without, so the letter is left out

parts.note: Tennyson's poem begins 'Come into the garden, Maud', so Maud is the woman invited

explanation.surface: A woman asked into a garden that lacks good firm earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The allusion is to Tennyson's line 'Come into the garden, Maud', also a well-known Victorian parlour song.
explanation.definitionFit: Mud is wet, soft earth, the squelchy ground after rain.

clue.text: Old city ceremony starts to excite individuals immensely

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial display

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: An ancient city's rituals thrill people enormously.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was a Roman city near Naples buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Stuffy girl I embarrassed

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
embarrassment makes you go red

explanation.surface: A prim young woman confesses her blushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffy' looks like a description of the girl, but means a room lacking fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: A room not aired lacks ventilation, so it is close and airless.

clue.text: Gesture of acceptance or refusal received finally

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of received

explanation.surface: A sign of yes or no was given in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A nod of the head signals agreement or approval.

clue.text: Push out old boy over time getting ill-mannered

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil
rude means impolite, ill-mannered

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy, rude with age, is thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to thrust something forward or make it stick out.

clue.text: Come to an end, being dismissed by umpire

definitions.meaning: to be used up or exhausted, as supplies do
in cricket, a batsman is out when the ball breaks the wicket before he reaches the crease

explanation.surface: A batsman's innings ends when the umpire raises his finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies or time can be exhausted; in cricket the same phrase names a dismissal while running between wickets.

clue.text: Sketchy summary that's not entirely accurate

indicators.note: not entirely means one letter short of the full word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: precise means exact, accurate

explanation.surface: A rough outline that isn't wholly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis gives only the main points of a text, an outline condensing it.

clue.text: High-up person to abuse king

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly
R, for Rex, is the Latin abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A senior figure moves to insult the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-up person' looks like a VIP, but is a roofer working up on the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A slater lays slates on roofs, so the job is done at height.

clue.text: Fellow getting into shelter turned up in coat

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the whole is read from bottom to top
getting into means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man ducking into a shelter showed up wearing a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' gives LEMANE, which 'turned up' then reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy layer of paint or glaze applied as a protective covering.

clue.text: Remarkable bird tweeting initially having been caught

indicators.note: having been caught means trapped inside, so the letter goes within the bird

parts.note: the starling is a common songbird

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of tweeting

explanation.surface: A notable bird was heard chirping before being trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means surprising enough to make one take notice, striking.

clue.text: Old rocker back in Paris is generating hate

indicators.note: back means turned the other way round, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British rock and roll fan
est is the French for is

explanation.surface: An ageing rock fan who has returned to Paris is stirring up loathing.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe or dislike intensely.

clue.text: Speed of soldiers maybe, intelligent when confronting the enemy

parts.note: quick means mentally sharp, intelligent
the saying 'time is the enemy' gives time

explanation.surface: Clever soldiers march fast when facing the foe.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick time is the military marching pace, normally about 120 steps a minute.

clue.text: Number getting cross twice in ancient Rome

definitions.text: Number getting cross twice in ancient Rome

parts.words: Number getting cross twice in ancient Rome
parts.note: a cross looks like the letter X, and two of them in Roman numerals make a score

explanation.surface: A figure who got angry twice in classical Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry, but is the X shape; XX is the Roman numeral that the definition 'Number' describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman numeral XX stands for two tens, the number a score.

clue.text: Not forced to have floral decoration, as it would seem

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
surely is used to state what seems certain

explanation.surface: Someone at ease is apparently wearing a garland.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisurely describes an unhurried, relaxed pace, done without pressure.
